children: Jefferies says it sees the Board of Trade as "the single possible deliverable," from the summit between President Trump and Chinese leader Xi. Agreed in May, the mechanism cuts tariffs toward most-favored-nation levels on $30 billion of goods in each direction, scoped to non-sensitive items, the analysts say in a note. They are optimistic that Board of Trade will be emphasized as a win by both sides because they say it's the only item that doesn't concede anything strategic. "Everything else runs into incentives neither leader will override before November. Taiwan, Japan, Iran and the Russia sanctions bill stay unresolved but set the risk backdrop." (patrick.sheridan@wsj.com)
